title: An Unusual Login
speaker: Joshua

ui.guide: Click a row to look at it
ui.monologue_hint: Press Enter or click to continue

messages.wrong_default: This looks normal. It does not tell me what happened.
messages.already_noted: I already wrote this one down. It is part of the story.

all_clues_found_monologue: That is enough proof. Someone got into Anna's account, took her payroll file, and sent it away. Time to write my report.

entries.title: Weekly company news
entries.detail:
From: Office News
To: All staff
Time: 07:30

This week: a new coffee machine, a charity bake sale on Friday, and a welcome to our new intern.
entries.monologue_wrong: Only office news. It will not help with the case.

entries.title: Lunch menu this week
entries.detail:
From: Facilities
To: All staff
Time: 08:00

Here is this week's lunch menu:
Mon: chicken rice
Tue: vegetable curry
Wed: fish and chips
Thu: pasta
Fri: pizza day
entries.monologue_wrong: Just a lunch menu. Nothing to do with the problem.

entries.title: Meeting moved to 9:30
entries.detail:
From: Ben Nguyen
To: The team
Time: 08:10

Hi all, our morning meeting is moving to 9:30 today. See you there.
entries.monologue_wrong: Ben is only moving a meeting. Nothing odd about that.

entries.title: Printer on floor 2 is fixed
entries.detail:
From: Helpdesk
To: All staff
Time: 08:20

The printer on floor 2 is working again. Sorry for the trouble.
entries.monologue_wrong: A fixed printer is good news, but it is not what I am looking for.

cells: I was not at work last night
entries.title: I was not at work last night
entries.detail:
From: Anna Reyes
To: IT Help
Time: 08:42

Hi, I got a message saying my account signed in at 2:43 this morning. But I was asleep at home! I did not sign in. Please can you check what happened?
entries.note: Anna was asleep at home, but her account signed in at night.
entries.monologue_correct: Anna was asleep at home, but her account signed in. So someone else is using her account.

entries.title: Yearly safety training
entries.detail:
From: HR
To: All staff
Time: 08:50

A reminder to finish your yearly safety training by the end of the month. It only takes 20 minutes.
entries.monologue_wrong: A training reminder everyone gets. It has nothing to do with last night.

entries.title: Nightly backup finished
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
Where: Backup room

The nightly backup finished on time. It saves a spare copy of the company's files. This happens every single night.
entries.monologue_wrong: The backup runs every night. That is normal.

entries.title: Someone connected from far away
entries.detail:
Time: 05:00
Where: Ben's computer
Who: IT Helpdesk (a trusted team)

The IT team connected to Ben's computer from their own office to install updates. They do this every week at 5 AM, and Ben was told about it.
entries.monologue_wrong: That sounds scary, but it is just IT updating Ben's computer. They do it every week.

entries.title: Virus scan finished
entries.detail:
Time: 06:00
Where: All computers

The weekly virus scan finished. It checks for bad programs. It found nothing new.
entries.monologue_wrong: A normal weekly scan. It does not explain the sign-in.

entries.title: Printer restarted
entries.detail:
Time: 07:45
Where: Printer, floor 2

The printer on floor 2 restarted by itself after the repair. It is working again.
entries.monologue_wrong: A printer restarting is not suspicious. Printers do that all the time.

entries.title: Anna's office computer
entries.detail:
Name: WS-ANNA
Owner: Anna Reyes
Status: Known

This is Anna's computer at her desk. It was switched off at 6 PM yesterday and stayed off all night.
entries.monologue_wrong: Anna's own computer was off all night. Good to know, but it does not show what happened by itself.

entries.title: Ben's office computer
entries.detail:
Name: WS-BEN
Owner: Ben Nguyen
Status: Known

Ben's computer at his desk. It is on the company list and works normally.
entries.monologue_wrong: Ben's normal computer. Nothing odd here.

entries.title: Carla's office computer
entries.detail:
Name: WS-CARLA
Owner: Carla Patel
Status: Known

Carla's computer at her desk. It is on the company list and works normally.
entries.monologue_wrong: Carla's normal computer. Nothing odd here.

entries.title: A new computer was added
entries.detail:
Name: WS-INTERN
Owner: Intern desk
Status: New

IT added this computer yesterday for the new intern. IT wrote it on the company list, so it is a known computer.
entries.monologue_wrong: A new computer, but IT added it on purpose and wrote it on the list. It is fine.

entries.title: The shared printer
entries.detail:
Name: PRINTER-2
Owner: Shared by everyone on floor 2
Status: Known

The printer on floor 2. It is on the company list.
entries.monologue_wrong: Just the shared printer. It is not part of this.

entries.title: Anna signed in from a computer nobody knows
entries.detail:
Time: 02:43
Person: Anna Reyes
Signed in from: a computer named UNKNOWN-7F3A
Result: it worked

Nobody in the company has added this computer to the list. Anna's own computer was switched off at the time.
entries.note: At 2:43 AM her account was used from a computer nobody knows.
entries.monologue_correct: Anna's account signed in from a computer nobody knows. That is not her computer, and it is not on our list.

entries.title: Ben signed in at the office
entries.detail:
Time: 07:52
Person: Ben Nguyen
Signed in from: his office computer
Result: it worked

Ben signs in around this time every morning.
entries.monologue_wrong: Ben signed in from his own desk in the morning, like always.

entries.title: Carla signed in at the office
entries.detail:
Time: 08:05
Person: Carla Patel
Signed in from: her office computer
Result: it worked

Carla signs in around this time every morning.
entries.monologue_wrong: Carla signed in from her own desk. That is completely normal.

entries.title: Dan typed a wrong password
entries.detail:
Time: 08:11
Person: Dan Kim
Signed in from: his office computer
Result: wrong password

Dan typed his password wrong once. He got it right a few seconds later.
entries.monologue_wrong: Dan mistyped his password once, then got it right. Everyone does that sometimes.

entries.title: Anna signed in at the office
entries.detail:
Time: 08:30
Person: Anna Reyes
Signed in from: her office computer
Result: it worked

Anna came to work and signed in from her own desk like normal.
entries.monologue_wrong: This is the real Anna, at her own desk, in the morning. It looks normal.

entries.title: The payroll file was copied
entries.detail:
Time: 02:52
Person: Anna Reyes (her account)
Action: made a copy
File: the payroll file

This file lists what every worker is paid, so it is private. Only the finance team should open it.
entries.note: At 2:52 AM the private payroll file was copied.
entries.monologue_correct: Someone copied the private payroll file, nine minutes after the strange sign-in. That is what they were after.

entries.title: The staff handbook was opened
entries.detail:
Time: 07:50
Person: Carla Patel
Action: opened
File: the staff handbook

Carla looked something up in the staff handbook. Anyone can open it.
entries.monologue_wrong: Anyone can open the staff handbook. It is not private.

entries.title: Meeting notes were opened
entries.detail:
Time: 08:15
Person: Carla Patel
Action: opened
File: meeting notes

Carla read the notes from last week's team meeting.
entries.monologue_wrong: Carla read some meeting notes. That is a normal thing to do at work.

entries.title: A new company logo was added
entries.detail:
Time: 08:35
Person: Dan Kim
Action: added a new file
File: the company logo

Dan added the new company logo so the team can use it.
entries.monologue_wrong: Dan only added a logo picture. It is not private and it is not part of this.

entries.title: The budget sheet was opened
entries.detail:
Time: 08:40
Person: Ben Nguyen
Action: opened
File: the budget sheet

Ben opened the budget sheet. This is part of his normal work.
entries.monologue_wrong: Ben opened the budget sheet in the morning, during work. That is his normal job.

network.label: NETWORK
network.title: NETWORK > WHAT WENT IN AND OUT

entries.title: Files were saved to the backup server
entries.detail:
Time: 01:00
From: the file server
To: the backup server
Size: 9 GB

This is the nightly backup. It stays inside the company, and it happens every night.
entries.monologue_wrong: That is the nightly backup. It stays inside the company, so it is fine.

entries.title: Information was sent outside the company
entries.detail:
Time: 02:52
From: the file server
To: a place outside the company that we have never talked to
Size: 48 MB

This computer normally never sends anything outside. It happened right after the payroll file was copied.
entries.note: At 2:52 AM information was sent to a computer outside the company.
entries.monologue_correct: Information was sent to a place outside the company that we never talk to. They took the file and sent it away.

entries.title: Ben's computer downloaded an update
entries.detail:
Time: 03:10
From: Ben's computer
To: the software update website
Size: 120 MB

The computer downloaded its usual software update. It does this every week.
entries.monologue_wrong: A normal software update. Every computer does that.

entries.title: The mail server got new emails
entries.detail:
Time: 07:15
From: the mail server
To: our email service
Size: 6 MB

The mail server picked up the morning's emails. It does this all day.
entries.monologue_wrong: That is just email arriving, like every morning.

entries.title: The file server
entries.detail:
Name: File server
Job: keeps the company's shared files
Status: running
Busy: 27%

This is where files like the payroll file are kept. It is running normally.
entries.monologue_wrong: The file server is running fine. The problem is who used it, not the server.

entries.title: The mail server
entries.detail:
Name: Mail server
Job: sends and gets the company's email
Status: running
Busy: 18%

It is running normally.
entries.monologue_wrong: The mail server is running normally. Nothing wrong here.

entries.title: The backup server
entries.detail:
Name: Backup server
Job: keeps spare copies of the company's files
Status: running
Busy: 5%

It is running normally.
entries.monologue_wrong: The backup server is quiet and working. It does not show a problem.

entries.title: The sign-in server
entries.detail:
Name: Sign-in server
Job: checks people's passwords when they sign in
Status: running
Busy: 12%

It checked every sign-in last night, including the one at 2:43. It is working correctly.
entries.monologue_wrong: The sign-in server did its job. The question is who was really signing in.

report.title: REPORT.exe > WHAT HAPPENED?
report.intro: Fill in the blanks to tell what happened. Drag a word into a blank, or click a word and then click a blank.
report.help: Keyboard: Tab to move. Enter picks up a word. Enter on a blank puts it there.
report.text: Late at night, someone used {1} to sign in from {2}. They copied {3} and then sent it to {4}.

messages.prompt: Read your notes, then fill in every blank.
messages.picked: Now click a blank to put "{word}" there.
messages.some_wrong: {right} of {total} are right. These blanks were wrong: {wrong_blanks}. Those words went back to the tray. Read your notes and try again.
messages.none_right: None of these fit yet. The words went back to the tray. Read your notes and try again.
messages.solved: Yes! That is exactly what happened. We know how they got in.

report.solved_explanation: This is called credential abuse: someone uses a real person's password to sneak in. It is hard to spot because the sign-in looks real.

next.title: MONITORING
next.description: Watch the system as it runs. Report the activity that looks wrong, but do not report normal activity. Correct reports earn Security Points to spend on defenses.
